analysis: The sampled-softmax trial completed successfully but underperformed the prior balanced-BCE ConvRec: pinned-host macro validation HR@10 fell from 0.5387 to 0.4987, a decrease of 0.0400. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.575, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.555, Electronics 0.360, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.505. Electronics declined from the reported prior 0.365 to 0.360, so this experiment did not support the hypothesis that stronger candidate competition would improve that category. Other prior category scores were not supplied, so their individual changes cannot be established. The result disfavors this exact loss replacement under the retained training setup; it does not establish that sampled softmax is generally inferior or identify the cause of the regression. Allocated GPU time was 315.56 seconds.
code_summary: One independent ConvRec model per category, with 96-dimensional tied item embeddings, jointly learned item bias, maximum sequence length 64, dropout 0.25, and four residual causal convolution blocks with dilations 1, 2, 4, and 8. Each block uses two causal convolutions, layer normalization, GELU, dropout, and padding masks. Only ranking_loss changed: mean unscaled sampled-softmax cross-entropy over one positive and 256 shared uniform negative draws, retaining duplicate negatives and masking positive collisions. Training retained random-prefix sampling, a 2048-position loss cap, seed 42, AdamW, warmup/cosine learning-rate schedule, gradient clipping, default 200 epochs, validation every five epochs plus the first/final epoch, 35-epoch early stopping, and one validation-selected checkpoint per category. Supplied splits, dataset routing, trial-local artifacts, and predictor writer remained unchanged. Prediction loads exactly one checkpoint for each category; no ensembles or separately fitted scores are used.
